name: Mary Frances Vantine
notable_stories: She was previously married at age 15 to a man named Clark and had one child, Clay C. Clark, who was given up for adoption and raised by neighbors before she married John Wesley Adams
Previously married at 15 to Ephraim Clark; had son Clay Clark
milestones: Married John Wesley Adams (m. 3 Jan 1866, Chariton County, MO)
locations: Mt Olivet Cemetery, Marceline, Linn County, Missouri
sources: Descendants of Jose Pierre Adams, compiled by William W. "Bill" Allen (2 April 2011 edition)
Newspaper clippings and obituaries in Bill Allen’s family document (2011)
Family research emails, 2011–2013 (John and Barbara Adams with Irma Kulp Zacher, George F. Adams, Bill Allen and others)
notes: First husband now named: Ephraim Clark (prior sources said 'a man named Clark').
Preparer (Bill Allen) notes she was his great-great-grandmother [Bill Allen, Descendants of Jose Pierre Adams, 2011, line 4149]
Photo caption names her 'Mary Frances VanTyne (Clark) Adams' (spelling variant VanTyne; surnames Clark and Adams) [Bill Allen, Descendants of Jose Pierre Adams, 2011, line 6025]

Open question: Mary Frances Vantine (Adams): she married Ephraim Clark at 15 and was barely 16 when he died at the end of the Civil War (1865), which conflicts with her tree birth of Oct 1844 and with Clay C. Clark's tree birth of 1860. [Family research emails, email 15, 16, 04]
